summary_for_children: Surah An-Nur teaches good manners in the home and in society: asking permission before entering, modesty, and not spreading rumours. It describes Allah's light with the beautiful example of a lamp in a niche.
environment_concept: Doors that open after greeting (24:27), a glass lamp in a niche like a bright star (24:35), a blessed olive grove (24:35), a mirage plain (24:39), a dark sea (24:40) and birds with spread wings (24:41).
architecture_and_scenery: Courtyard house with closed doors that open only after greeting, a central niche with a glass lamp, an olive grove, a shimmering mirage plain and a stormy night sea.

palette.lighting: One radiant lamp, warm interior glow; outside, harsh mirage light and deep sea darkness
palette.atmosphere: Still indoors; heat haze and thunder outside

primary_mechanic.text: Guide sunlight with mirrors through geometric windows, and knock and wait for welcome before entering a house (24:27); the lamp parable (24:35) stays a reading.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Light
story_library.children_narration: Surah An-Nur teaches us about respectful behavior, privacy, modesty, and treating people fairly. It also contains a beautiful parable involving light, a lamp, and a niche. Light helps us think about the importance of guidance, but Allah is not represented by anything we create.

world_idea.title: The Architecture of Light
world_idea.description: Navigate beautifully designed buildings using reflected light and geometric openings. Practice knocking before entering, respecting privacy, and learning about responsible speech.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The light parable (24:35) is about Allah. It stays a reading; mirrors and light are never used to stand for Allah.
